title: Resources and Development — Class 10 CBSE Geography
subject: Social Science (Geography)

slides.title: Resources and Development
slides.speaker_notes: From rocks to soil to development.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
What is a resource?
bullets: Anything in environment that satisfies a need.
Conditions: tech access + econ feasibility + cultural acceptance.
Stone in a garden — resource? It depends!

slides.title: Classification — origin & exhaustibility
bullets: Renewable can still run out if over-used (forests).

slides.title: Classification — ownership & status
bullets: RESERVES — tech ready, use postponed (dam water).

slides.title: Sustainable development + Rio 1992
bullets: Rio Earth Summit 1992 — 100+ heads of state.
Agenda 21 — global plan + every local body.

slides.title: Resource planning in India
bullets: Step 2: planning structure with technology + institutions.
Step 3: integrate with national development plan.
Jharkhand minerals; Rajasthan sun; Arunachal water; Ladakh tourism.

slides.title: Soils — the living resource
bullets: Soil takes millions of years to form a few cm.
Formed by relief, parent rock, climate, vegetation, time.

slides.title: Major soils of India
bullets: ALLUVIAL — northern plains; Bangar (old) + Khadar (new); fertile.
LATERITE — heat + heavy rain; tea, coffee, cashew.
ARID — sandy, saline; FOREST — hilly forested areas.

slides.title: Soil erosion
bullets: SHEET erosion → topsoil washed off slope.

slides.title: Soil conservation
bullets: STRIP CROPPING — grass strips between crop strips.
SHELTER BELTS — rows of trees, stabilised dunes.

slides.title: You try (5 min)
bullets: 1. Classify hydrogen as a resource — by status.
2. Two states most affected by over-irrigation.
4. Two soil-conservation methods used in your region.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q2. Bangar vs Khadar — which is more fertile?
Q3. Laterite — humus rich or poor?
Q4. Strip cropping — what is it?

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Four classifications — origin / exhaustibility / ownership / status.
Land use & degradation patterns by Indian region.
Six soils — alluvial, black, red, laterite, arid, forest.
Erosion countered by contour, terrace, strip cropping, shelter belts.
